subtitle: Shrine, Silence and the Making of a Warrior Saint

panels.shot: epic split composition, half showing a medieval shrine at Bahraich, half a hazy battlefield made of fading silhouettes
panels.action: Suheldev of Bahraich stands on one side and Ghazi Miyan on the other, both half-formed like figures of mist, behind them the domed shrine of Bahraich rises against a dusky sky, its steps crowded with tiny, indistinct worshippers.

dialogue.text: At Bahraich, a shrine stands firm, but the battle around Suheldev and Ghazi Miyan lives only in memory and a book written six hundred years later.

i18n.hi: बहराइच में दरगाह अडिग है, पर सुहेलदेव–गाज़ी मियाँ की जंग बस यादों में है, और सैकड़ों साल बाद लिखी एक किताब में।

panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of the Sarayu-Ghagra plains around Bahraich, dense with forest patches, fields and a winding river, under a hazy North Indian sun.

dialogue.text: The legend says that around 1033, the fields near Bahraich shook with a great battle between Suheldev and the young warrior Ghazi Miyan, Salar Masud.

i18n.hi: कहानी है कि करीब 1033 में बहराइच के खेत सुहेलदेव और जवान सिपहसलार गाज़ी मियाँ, सालार मसूद की भयंकर लड़ाई से काँप उठे।

panels.action: In the foreground, Ghazi Miyan as a young mounted warrior in simple mail looks toward a distant horizon; in the background, faint and farther, Suheldev stands on a rise, cloaked, watching with a cautious, unreadable gaze.

dialogue.text: In village songs, in shrine tales, the story is clear: the ghazi from Ghazni rode east; a local raja rose to stop him; their clash forged the land’s destiny.

i18n.hi: गाँव के गीतों, दरगाह की कहानी में बात साफ है: ग़ज़नी का गाज़ी पूरब चला; एक देसी राजा उसे रोकने उठा; उनकी टक्कर ने इस धरती की तकदीर गढ़ी।

panels.action: Hundreds of anonymous pilgrims across time walk toward a modest but bustling shrine complex at Bahraich, some with green flags, some with flowers, some bareheaded, the air heavy with dust and incense.

dialogue.text: What we can see, even now, is the shrine at Bahraich: a place where for centuries people have come to seek the warrior saint’s barakat, his blessing.

i18n.hi: आज भी जो दिखता है, वो है बहराइच की दरगाह: सदियों से लोग यहाँ जंगी पीर की बरकत, उसकी दुआ लेने आते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on an old manuscript with ghostly figures hovering
panels.action: An aged Persian manuscript lies open on a wooden stand, its script finely inked; faint translucent images of Ghazi Miyan and Suheldev hover above the page like memories summoned by the text.

dialogue.text: But when we search for the battle itself, for the marching armies and clashing swords, the trail leads to one main book: the Mirat-i-Masudi of Abdur Rahman Chishti, written around 1620.

i18n.hi: पर जब असली जंग ढूँढते हैं, फ़ौजों की चाल, तलवारों की टनकार, तो राह बस एक बड़ी किताब तक जाती है: अब्दुर रहमान चिश्ती की मिरात-ए-मसूदी, जो लगभग 1620 की है।

panels.action: Abdur Rahman Chishti, depicted as an elderly Mughal-era scholar, sits cross-legged by lamplight, writing on a long sheet of paper while a faint, idealised vision of Ghazi Miyan stands approvingly behind him.

dialogue.text: Chishti calls his work a mirror of Masud, a hagiography, a saint’s life. He writes five, maybe six centuries after the events he describes, shaping miracle and battle into a single tale.

i18n.hi: चिश्ती अपनी किताब को ‘मसूद का आईना’ कहता है, यानि एक औलिया की जिंदगी। वो घटनाओं के पाँच–छः सौ साल बाद लिखता है, करामात और जंग को एक ही दास्तान में बुनता है।

panels.shot: wide imaginary battlefield tableau, slightly desaturated to feel unreal
panels.action: An expansive field scene of two facing forces is shown like a faded painting: Ghazi Miyan’s banner on one side, Suheldev’s on the other, but the soldiers’ forms blur at the edges as if made of smoke.

dialogue.text: In the Mirat, Masud marches from Ghazni, takes holy war eastward, and falls at Bahraich in a fierce clash with a Hindu king named Suheldev. This is the battle as devotion remembers it.

i18n.hi: मिरात में मसूद ग़ज़नी से कूच करता है, जिहाद को पूरब तक लाता है, और बहराइच में सुहेलदेव नाम के हिंदू राजा से ज़ोरदार भिड़ंत में गिर पड़ता है। यही जंग भक्ति की याद में बसती है।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Chishti’s writing hand, then cut to a blank space on another parchment
panels.action: One panel of the scene shows Chishti’s hand firmly inscribing the words ‘Bahraich’ and ‘Masud’; beside it, a second sheet marked ‘1030s’ remains blank, emphasising absence.

dialogue.text: Yet for historians, one late book is not a chain. They ask: who else, nearer that time, saw this battle and wrote its name?

i18n.hi: पर इतिहासकारों के लिए एक देर की किताब पूरी कड़ी नहीं बनती। वो पूछते हैं: उस दौर के करीब और किसने ये जंग देखी और उसका नाम लिखा?

panels.action: Al-Biruni, in simple robes, sits calmly amid scrolls and astrolabes, looking over a palm-leaf manuscript of Indian lore, through an open jharokha to a tranquil landscape beyond.

dialogue.text: Al-Biruni, writing around 1030 in the shadow of Mahmud of Ghazni’s campaigns, describes India’s rivers, sciences, kings and wars. He is our sharpest early witness to that age.

i18n.hi: अल-बिरूनी, जो करीब 1030 में महमूद ग़ज़नी की फतहों की छाँव में लिख रहा था, भारत की नदियाँ, इल्म, बादशाह और जंगें सब दर्ज करता है। वही उस दौर का सबसे तेज गवाह है।

panels.shot: close-up on Al-Biruni’s thoughtful face, eyes lowered
panels.action: A close view of Al-Biruni’s lined, reflective face as he pauses mid-writing, quill held lightly, the lamplight catching the seriousness in his eyes.

dialogue.text: If a prince from Ghazni had led a vast, decisive jihad deep into the eastern plains and fallen at Bahraich, we might expect some echo in his pages. There is none.

i18n.hi: अगर ग़ज़नी का कोई शाहज़ादा विशाल, निर्णायक जिहाद लेकर बहुत दूर पूरब आया होता और बहराइच में शहीद होता, तो हम उम्मीद करते उसकी किताब में कहीं न कहीं हल्की गूँज मिलेगी। वो नहीं है।

panels.shot: montage wide shot of different chronicles on a shelf
panels.action: A shelf of bound chronicles and loose folios from Ghaznavid and Indian courts stands in semi-darkness; the camera angle emphasises their spines, some labelled by era, most silent on Bahraich.

dialogue.text: Other earlier chronicles, Persian and Indian, list campaigns of Mahmud and his successors. They know Ghazni, Lahore, Somnath, Multan. They do not speak of Salar Masud’s war at Bahraich.

i18n.hi: और भी पहले की तवारीख, फ़ारसी और देसी, महमूद और उसके वारिसों की फतहें गिनती हैं। उन्हें ग़ज़नी, लाहौर, सोमनाथ, मुल्तान सब याद हैं। सालार मसूद की बहराइच वाली जंग का ज़िक्र नहीं।

panels.shot: pattern-interrupt close-up on an empty battlefield
panels.action: A calm, empty stretch of fields near Bahraich at dawn, only dew on grass and a faint mist above the soil, no armies, no banners, just silence and birds in the distance.

dialogue.text: The legend is loud; the land is quiet. No inscriptions, no copper plates, no dated victory edicts from Suheldev or Masud fix a day or place for this clash.

i18n.hi: कहानी ऊँची है; ज़मीन खामोश। न कोई शिला-लेख, न ताम्रपत्र, न सुहेलदेव या मसूद की तारीख़वाली फतह-घोषणा जो इस भिड़ंत की तय दिन-ज़मीन बताए।

panels.shot: wide shrine courtyard, time-lapse effect implied
panels.action: The courtyard of Ghazi Miyan’s shrine at Bahraich is shown across changing light, from dawn to dusk, as generations of anonymous visitors file in and out, some Hindu, some Muslim, some difficult to place.

dialogue.text: What does endure from the eleventh century is not a battlefield, but a cult. By the late medieval period, Masud is venerated here as Ghazi Miyan, the warrior saint of Bahraich.

i18n.hi: जिस चीज़ ने ग्यारहवीं सदी से टिक कर जिया, वो मैदान जंग नहीं, एक मज़ार की श्रद्धा है। देर-मध्यकाल तक मसूद यहीं गाज़ी मियाँ, बहराइच के जंगी पीर की तरह पूजे जाते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot at the shrine interior
panels.action: Inside the shrine, a simple cloth-covered tomb lies under a low dome; Ghazi Miyan is seen as a gentle, devotional presence in the background, while faint rural worshippers kneel or stand in quiet supplication.

dialogue.text: Shahid Amin shows how, over centuries, peasants and townsfolk made Masud their own, tying his story to local harvests, healings, feuds and vows, blending Arab-Turkic warrior and North Indian saint.

i18n.hi: शाहिद अमीन दिखाते हैं कि कैसे सदियों में किसानों और कस्बों ने मसूद को अपना बनाया, उसकी कहानी को अपने खेत, मन्नत, झगड़े, चंगाई से जोड़ा, अरब–तुर्क जंगजू को उत्तर भारतीय पीर में घोला।

panels.shot: crossfade shot between shrine and rural village square
panels.action: The image crossfades: on one side the Bahraich shrine, on the other a village square where a bard recites under a tree, villagers listening as a heroic Suheldev figure rises in their imagination.

dialogue.text: As the saint’s fame spreads, another memory grows in the villages: Suheldev, the local king who, in their counter-story, did not bow to Ghazi Miyan but defeated him.

i18n.hi: जैसे-जैसे पीर की शोहरत फैलती है, वैसे-वैसे गाँवों में एक और याद पनपती है: सुहेलदेव, देसी राजा जो, उनकी उलट कहानी में, गाज़ी मियाँ के आगे झुका नहीं, बल्कि उसे हरा गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a village bard with animated silhouettes
panels.action: A village storyteller sits on a low platform, gesturing as shadowy silhouettes of Suheldev and Ghazi Miyan fight above him, his audience of men and women leaning forward, spellbound.

dialogue.speaker: suheldev_and_salar_masud
dialogue.text: “We remember him as the one who did not yield,” a villager says softly.

i18n.hi: “हम उसे उसी के रूप में याद रखते हैं जो झुका नहीं,” एक गाँव वाला धीमे से कहता है।

panels.shot: two-part frame, one side hagiographer, other side modern historian
panels.action: On the left, Abdur Rahman Chishti continues to write his saint’s life; on the right, a modern historian like Shahid Amin sits at a desk with books and field notes, looking from the Mirat to a village interview transcript.

dialogue.text: Between Chishti’s hagiography and later village counter-memory, two figures emerge: Ghazi Miyan the martyr saint, and Suheldev the resistant king. Both are products of faith, fear and hope as much as of fact.

i18n.hi: चिश्ती की औलिया-कथा और बाद की गाँवों की प्रतिकथा के बीच दो साये उभरते हैं: शहीद गाज़ी मियाँ, और सुहेलदेव, डटकर लड़ने वाला राजा। दोनों उतने ही आस्था, डर और आस के हैं जितना कि हकीकत के।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Suheldev and Ghazi Miyan facing each other, half-solid, half-translucent
panels.action: In a dreamlike space, Suheldev and Ghazi Miyan stand facing each other, their lower bodies solid but their upper halves turning into script and song notes that drift upward into darkness.

dialogue.text: Modern scholarship does not confirm Suheldev’s battle with Masud as a proven event. It studies instead how different communities used their names to speak of conquest, loss and courage.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक शोध सुहेलदेव–मसूद की जंग को पक्की, साबित घटना नहीं मानता। वो ज़्यादा ये देखता है कि अलग-अलग बिरादरियों ने उनके नामों से फतह, हार और हिम्मत पर बात कैसे की।

panels.shot: final wide shot of Bahraich landscape with shrine in distance
panels.action: The Bahraich shrine sits small but distinct on the horizon as the camera pulls back to show the surrounding plains, villages, and a quiet river winding past under a vast sky.

dialogue.text: The shrine is real; the legend around it is powerful; the battle it tells of is uncertain. To walk this ground with honesty is to honour memory, yet never mistake it for proof.

i18n.hi: दरगाह सच है; उसके इर्द–गिर्द की दास्तान बेहद ताकतवर; जिसकी जंग वो सुनाती है, वो अनिश्चित। इस धरती पर ईमानदारी से चलना मतलब याद को सलाम करना, पर उसे सबूत समझने की गलती न करना।

title_i18n.en: Bahraich and the Battle Made of Memory
title_i18n.hi: बहराइच और यादों से बनी जंग

subtitle_i18n.en: Shrine, Silence and the Making of a Warrior Saint
subtitle_i18n.hi: दरगाह, सन्नाटा और एक जंगी सूफी की साधना
